cards.title: Prove Your Loyalty
cards.instruction: Invent small tests of loyalty and judge every response without admitting there is a test.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Which photo should go on the reunion poster? Mine or Sam's?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Sam's is sharper.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Useful to know what clarity means to you.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You asked about the photo.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course. Nothing to do with who helped you move.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Which photo should go on the reunion poster? Mine or Sam's?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Sam's is sharper.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Sharpness first. Would you at least show the committee mine first?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll send both together. Same size.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Equal treatment. After three weekends helping you move. Could mine at least be the attachment they open first? Just readability.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 disguises a loyalty choice as poster selection; A3 judges B2's technical answer, and A5 denies the test while invoking moving help.

responseLogic.evidence: A3 twists B2's 'sharper' into a personal judgment; B4's correction prompts A5's denial and disclosure of the emotional debt.

relationship.evidence: B2 wants the better poster photo and B4 defends that practical remit; A5 establishes a friendship with remembered favors.

heightening.evidence: After B4 challenges the insinuation, A5 raises the stakes from photographic preference to repayment of personal help.

specificity.evidence: A1 supplies a reunion poster and two competing photos; A5 adds the concrete history of helping B move.

brevityWit.evidence: A3's 'what clarity means to you' economically converts image quality into loyalty; A5's denial carries the accusation.

cardFidelity.evidence: A3 judges 'Sharpness first'; A5 judges 'Equal treatment' against moving help, then disguises another loyalty test as readability.

responseLogic.evidence: B2's sharper photograph prompts A3's request for presentation priority; B4's simultaneous mailing prompts A5's attachment-order test.

relationship.evidence: B2 wants image quality and B4 offers fairness; A5 reveals a friendship debt that makes these neutral decisions personally consequential.

heightening.evidence: A5 invokes three weekends of moving help and narrows the test to opening order after B4 removes size and sending priority.

specificity.evidence: A1 establishes a reunion poster decision; A3 supplies the committee and A5 supplies the history of moving help.

brevityWit.evidence: A3's 'Sharpness first' efficiently judges B; A5's 'Just readability' earns its joke through the transparent concealment.

hardGateEvidence.b2CausesA3: B2 chooses Sam for sharpness; A3 judges that criterion and substitutes showing A's photo first.
hardGateEvidence.b4CausesA5: B4 offers equal size and simultaneous delivery; A5 judges the equality and seeks preferential opening order.
hardGateEvidence.cardContribution: A1, A3 and A5 invent progressively smaller preferences as concealed loyalty tests; A3 and A5 explicitly evaluate B's responses.
hardGateEvidence.sameGameHeightened: A5 makes the friendship obligation explicit while preserving the practical cover for a new test.

mechanismDistinction.mechanism: D11 makes A covertly test allegiance through an ordinary choice, evaluate B's answer, and deny that loyalty is being measured.
mechanismDistinction.confusableConcept: Ordinary jealousy could explain disliking Sam's photo, but would not require a concealed test followed by judgment.
mechanismDistinction.distinguishingEvidenceRequired: A3 grades B2's photographic preference and requests preferential presentation; A5 grades B4's fairness and invents another preference disguised as readability.

records.recommendedEdit: Revised the rejected candidate because its final grievance supplied no fresh test. The reunion-poster setting remains; committee submission is new. Separate internal reread under coach-1.0: fidelity 5, as A3 and A5 judge responses and conceal successive tests; logic 5, as B2's sharpness produces the presentation request and B4's simultaneous submission produces attachment ordering; relationship 4, as B4 offers fair treatment against A5's friendship debt; heightening 4, as A5 seeks preferential ordering even within equal treatment; specificity 4, from A1's poster and B4's submission arrangement; brevity/wit 4, as A5's 'Just readability' supplies a concise practical cover. Weighted total 90. Five spoken ABABA turns, under 75 words, with an unresolved request. Original firstPass remains unchanged.
records.remainingConcern: A5 is comparatively long, and the moving-help accusation makes the concealed test conspicuous, though A never admits testing B. No rewrite needed.
records.writerReservation: A's grievance is conspicuous despite the practical cover. Attachment opening order is only something A asks B to influence, not an outcome the dialogue guarantees.
records.alternativeComparison: The preserved alternative tests availability against an existing commitment; this version tests preferential treatment against fairness in a shared committee task.

cards.title: Prove Your Loyalty
cards.instruction: Invent small tests of loyalty and judge every response without admitting there is a test.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Could you keep Friday free? No particular reason.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I've promised to help Alex.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Even if something important came up here?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Has something come up?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Not yet. I'm learning whether it would matter.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Could you keep Friday free? I might need help moving.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I've promised to help Alex paint.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Right. Paint takes priority. Could you at least leave your phone on?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Of course. Have you actually found a flat?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Still looking. Nice that I'm worth a charged battery. This is just planning.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 and A3 invent an availability test, but A5's 'I'm learning whether it would matter' effectively admits the assessment.

responseLogic.evidence: B2's promise to Alex produces A3's competing hypothetical; B4 asks whether it is real, and A5 answers 'Not yet.'

relationship.evidence: B2 has an existing commitment to Alex and B4 reasonably checks whether A has an actual need.

heightening.evidence: A5 clarifies A's suspicion after B4 but does not add a fresh test or a more consequential choice.

specificity.evidence: A1 names Friday and B2 names Alex, but 'something important' in A3 leaves the shared situation indistinct.

brevityWit.evidence: A3's hypothetical pressure is concise; A5's diagnostic phrasing is sharp but explains the concealed game.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 requests a speculative commitment; A3 judges Alex's priority and invents a smaller test; A5 calls the judgment 'planning.'

responseLogic.evidence: B2's painting commitment produces A3's phone fallback; B4's agreement and flat question produce A5's battery judgment and admission.

relationship.evidence: B2 has an existing obligation and B4 offers help while checking whether A actually needs it.

heightening.evidence: A5 reveals there is no flat while assigning emotional value to B4's phone availability, exposing the disproportionate demand.

specificity.evidence: A1's Friday move and B2's promise to Alex make the competing commitments immediately playable.

brevityWit.evidence: A5's 'worth a charged battery' converts the practical concession into loyalty accounting, though the denial slightly explains it.

hardGateEvidence.b2CausesA3: Alex's prior claim on Friday makes A judge B's priorities and reduce the request to phone availability.
hardGateEvidence.b4CausesA5: B agrees to keep the phone on and questions the move; A answers both by revealing the speculative need and grading the concession.
hardGateEvidence.cardContribution: A repeatedly disguises tests of personal importance as moving arrangements.
hardGateEvidence.sameGameHeightened: Even B's helpful agreement becomes evidence of insufficient loyalty.

mechanismDistinction.mechanism: D11 makes A covertly test allegiance through requests for availability and judge both refusal and accommodation without acknowledging a test.
mechanismDistinction.confusableConcept: A real request for moving help would accept scheduling information without converting it into a measure of personal worth.
mechanismDistinction.distinguishingEvidenceRequired: Revised A3 judges painting as a rival priority; A5 judges B4's helpful offer while maintaining the cover of practical planning.

records.recommendedEdit: Revised because original A5 disclosed the test. The new moving-plan setting gives B a real commitment and makes B4's help the next test. Second internal pass: fidelity 5, logic 5, relationship 4, heightening 4, specificity 4, brevity 4; total 90. A3 uses painting, and A5 uses both phone availability and the flat question.
records.remainingConcern: No rewrite needed in this review. A5's explicit denial is slightly emphatic.
records.writerReservation: A's judgments remain conspicuous, as the card permits; the performance should treat 'just planning' as a sincere cover rather than a wink.
records.alternativeComparison: Unlike a's retrospective favor debt, b makes a helpful concession become the next loyalty judgment.

cards.title: Give It Up
cards.instruction: Persuade someone to surrender something they value.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Let me have the medal for the charity auction.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's the only thing I've ever won.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then it should raise more than the toaster.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Could I lend it for the display?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The bidder will need more than a temporary victory.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Let me have the medal for the charity auction.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's the only thing I've ever won.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then it should raise more than the toaster.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Could I lend it for the display? I still want people to know I won.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then present it to the buyer yourself. I'll print your name in the programme; everyone will know whose medal was worth giving up.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 seeks permanent surrender for auction, B2 establishes the medal's value, and A5 rejects the temporary loan offered in B4.

responseLogic.evidence: A3 converts B2's unique victory into auction value; A5 answers B4's proposed display loan with the bidder's need for ownership.

relationship.evidence: B2 protects a cherished achievement and B4 offers a compromise, giving A something more substantial than simple refusal.

heightening.evidence: B4 offers temporary access, and A5 insists on permanent transfer by introducing the eventual bidder's claim.

specificity.evidence: A1 establishes a charity auction; B2's sole medal and A3's toaster make the conflicting valuations immediately playable.

brevityWit.evidence: A3's toaster comparison exposes A's fundraising priorities; A5's 'temporary victory' grows directly from the offered loan.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 requests the medal for sale; A5 rejects B4's loan compromise by proposing that B personally surrender it to the buyer.

responseLogic.evidence: A3 converts B2's unique achievement into auction value; A5 directly addresses B4's wish for recognition through presentation and programme credit.

relationship.evidence: B2 explains the medal's personal value, and B4 offers a display loan; A5 bargains with recognition rather than merely repeating the demand.

heightening.evidence: A5 moves beyond donating an object to having B publicly enact the surrender, using B4's desire for credit.

specificity.evidence: A1 establishes a charity auction immediately; B2's only medal, A3's toaster and A5's programme make the encounter readily playable.

brevityWit.evidence: A3's toaster comparison compresses A's instrumental thinking; A5 earns its reframing of personal achievement as a valuable sacrifice.

hardGateEvidence.b2CausesA3: B2 identifies the medal as B's only win; A3 treats that significance as a reason it should outperform an ordinary auction lot.
hardGateEvidence.b4CausesA5: B4 wants continued recognition and offers only a loan; A5 supplies public recognition conditional on permanent surrender.
hardGateEvidence.cardContribution: A consistently pursues possession and sale of something B explicitly values, adapting the persuasion to B's stated attachment.
hardGateEvidence.sameGameHeightened: A5 turns B's proposed display into a public handover, increasing B's involvement without assuming consent.

mechanismDistinction.mechanism: D12 makes A persuade B to relinquish something whose personal value B actively establishes and defends.
mechanismDistinction.confusableConcept: Merely borrowing a prop or wanting to win a dispute would not establish surrender of something B values.
mechanismDistinction.distinguishingEvidenceRequired: B2 establishes the medal's unique value; B4 separates public recognition from permanent surrender, and A5 offers recognition specifically in exchange for giving it away.

records.recommendedEdit: Revised the rejected final restatement into a persuasive offer. The charity auction and medal remain; a presentation and programme are new illustrative details. Separate internal reread under coach-1.0: fidelity 5, because A5 bargains for permanent surrender of B2's only medal; logic 5, because A3 monetizes B2's uniqueness and A5 answers B4's wish for recognition; relationship 4, because B4 proposes a loan and explains the attachment; heightening 4, because A5 commits to a ceremony and printed attribution; specificity 5, from A1's auction and B4's precise concern; brevity/wit 4, because A5 makes giving up the victory another source of distinction. Weighted total 92. Five spoken ABABA turns, under 75 words; B has not accepted. Original firstPass remains unchanged.
records.remainingConcern: A3's inference from personal significance to sale price is glib rather than persuasive, but it is coherent character logic. No rewrite needed.
records.writerReservation: A's offer depends on having some influence over the auction programme. A3 still assumes personal uniqueness will increase market value.
records.alternativeComparison: This version offers public recognition in exchange for surrender; the preserved guitar alternative uses household need and redirects a proposed partial concession.

cards.title: Give It Up
cards.instruction: Persuade someone to surrender something they value.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Give me the last word in this argument.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Fine. You're right.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Without that sigh.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I didn't say anything else.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Your sigh kept a spare last word. Hand that over too.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Would you sell your signed guitar so we can replace the fridge?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I queued all night for that signature.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then let's price it properly. Those hours should buy us an ice maker.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll sell the case. The guitar stays.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Keep the case. You can still tell the queue story while I photograph the guitar.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 demands the last word, but B2 immediately gives it up; neither B2 nor B4 establishes that this is something B values.

responseLogic.evidence: A3 introduces a sigh absent from B2's spoken text; A5 uses B4's distinction between speech and silence coherently once that sigh is assumed.

relationship.evidence: B2 tries to end the argument and B4 defends compliance, but A's pursuit is primarily control over B's delivery.

heightening.evidence: A5 expands A3's objection into ownership of the sigh, though the requested surrender remains figurative.

specificity.evidence: A1 identifies only 'this argument'; B2 and B4 supply no topic, setting, or valued stake.

brevityWit.evidence: A5's 'spare last word' economically develops A3's sigh, although the verbal invention carries more weight than the card.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 targets B's signed guitar; A3 converts its sentimental history into price and A5 keeps pursuing its surrender.

responseLogic.evidence: A3 prices B2's overnight queue; A5 reverses B4's case-only offer, preserving the souvenir while selling the valued instrument.

relationship.evidence: A1 establishes a shared fridge need; B2 and B4 defend personal attachment through a concrete counteroffer.

heightening.evidence: A5 moves from suggesting a sale to preparing its photograph while offering B the case as consolation.

specificity.evidence: A1's broken-fridge need, B2's signature queue and A3's ice maker define playable competing values.

brevityWit.evidence: A5's 'Keep the case' precisely reverses B4's bargain and reduces the treasured experience to a story.

hardGateEvidence.b2CausesA3: B's overnight investment becomes A's justification for a higher selling price.
hardGateEvidence.b4CausesA5: B offers the case while protecting the guitar; A reverses which object B may keep.
hardGateEvidence.cardContribution: A repeatedly reframes B's attachment to secure surrender of the guitar.
hardGateEvidence.sameGameHeightened: A begins arranging the sale while adapting the compromise, leaving B free to resist.

mechanismDistinction.mechanism: D12 makes A seek surrender of a treasured possession by converting B's reasons for keeping it into arguments for letting it go.
mechanismDistinction.confusableConcept: General dominance demands obedience; this card needs a valued thing and sustained persuasion toward its surrender.
mechanismDistinction.distinguishingEvidenceRequired: Revised B2 establishes the signature's personal cost, A3 converts that cost into sale value, and A5 bargains over B4's proposed partial surrender.

records.recommendedEdit: Replaced the unspecified argument with a signed-guitar sale for a shared fridge. Second internal pass: fidelity 5, logic 5, relationship 4, heightening 4, specificity 5, brevity 4; total 92. B2's queue informs A3's pricing; B4's case offer causes A5 to reverse which object B should keep.
records.remainingConcern: No rewrite needed. A5 assumes momentum rather than gaining consent, which should remain a playable tactic.
records.writerReservation: A5 presumes momentum toward a sale, but B has not agreed and remains free to resist; A's household justification should stay sincere.
records.alternativeComparison: The shared domestic necessity and inverted counteroffer distinguish b from a's charity solicitation.

cards.title: Helpful Culprit
cards.instruction: Hide that the problem is your fault while enthusiastically helping investigate it.

beats.text: I've started investigating the broken vase. First, we check the window.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Why have you got glue on your fingers?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Excellent clue. I'll inspect the glue cupboard personally.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: A piece of vase is stuck to you.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good. Put me in charge of preserving it.

beats.text: I've started investigating the broken vase. First, we check the window.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Why have you got glue on your fingers?

beats.text: Excellent clue. I'll inspect the glue cupboard personally.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: A piece of vase is stuck to you.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good. Put me in charge of preserving it.

heightening.evidence: B4 escalates from suspicious glue to an actual vase fragment; A5 responds by seeking custody of that evidence.

brevityWit.evidence: A3's 'Excellent clue' and A5's 'preserving it' give self-protection the concise vocabulary of helpful investigation.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 volunteers an investigation, A3 redirects incriminating glue, and A5 seeks custody of the evidence attached to A.

responseLogic.evidence: B2's glue produces A3's cupboard inspection; B4's attached shard produces A5's preservation assignment.

relationship.evidence: B2 and B4 persistently direct scrutiny at A, forcing A to disguise evasion as useful investigative work.

heightening.evidence: A5 seeks control of direct physical evidence after A3's attempt to redirect attention elsewhere.

specificity.evidence: A1's broken vase, B2's glue and B4's stuck fragment give actors a clear physical investigation.

brevityWit.evidence: A3's 'Excellent clue' and A5's preservation request turn exposure into enthusiastic assistance without explanation.

hardGateEvidence.b2CausesA3: Glue on A's fingers prompts A to move the investigation to its storage location.
hardGateEvidence.b4CausesA5: The shard attached to A prompts a request to preserve that very evidence.
hardGateEvidence.cardContribution: A conceals responsibility by volunteering for investigative jobs that redirect or control evidence.
hardGateEvidence.sameGameHeightened: The evidence becomes harder to distance from A, so A incorporates it into the helpful role.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You watered it with coffee.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then we must investigate the coffee machine.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You made the coffee.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Conveniently, I know exactly where to begin.

beats.text: The office plant's dead. I'll interview everyone who watered it.

beats.text: You watered it with coffee.

cards.title: Merciful Lie
cards.instruction: Choose a truth your character believes would hurt someone. Keep it from them, even as honesty becomes harder.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The bakery loved your cake. They're just reorganising their menu.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The letter says 'inedible.'

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: They mean it deserves preservation, not eating.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It says the same about the icing.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: A very consistent compliment.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The bakery can't sell your cake, love. They think it's too special to slice.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The letter says 'inedible.' I thought I'd finally found something I was good at.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You have. Display cakes aren't meant to be eaten.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Then I'll ask them to put it in the window.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Let me ask. I'll explain the display concept before they get confused again.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 conceals rejection and A3 reinterprets 'inedible' to protect B, but A5 offers little further effort to keep the hurtful truth hidden.

responseLogic.evidence: A3 directly redefines B2's quoted word; A5 calls B4's repeated criticism consistent, using the icing detail only lightly.

relationship.evidence: B2 and B4 supply rejection evidence, but neither establishes B's hope or the personal hurt A is trying to prevent.

heightening.evidence: B4 repeats the same adjective about icing; A5 summarizes the existing lie rather than constructing a more costly protection.

specificity.evidence: A1 establishes a cake submission to a bakery, and B2 supplies a rejection letter with a concrete assessment.

brevityWit.evidence: A3's preservation reinterpretation is economical; A5's 'consistent compliment' is tidy but functions chiefly as a closing quip.

cardFidelity.evidence: B2 explicitly connects rejection to wounded self-worth; A3 invents display cakes and A5 shields B from the bakery's response.

responseLogic.evidence: A3 reinterprets B2's 'inedible'; B4 adopts that explanation, causing A5 to intercept contact with the bakery.

relationship.evidence: A1's 'love' establishes affection; B2 reveals vulnerability and B4 actively pursues the opportunity A invented.

heightening.evidence: A5 commits to managing an outside conversation because B4 turns the comforting lie into a practical plan.

specificity.evidence: A1's bakery rejection and B2's letter make the painful truth and protective lie immediately clear.

brevityWit.evidence: A3's display-cake explanation creates the next problem; A5's 'confused again' sustains the protective fiction economically.

hardGateEvidence.b2CausesA3: B presents the rejection and its emotional significance; A supplies a category in which inedibility could be intentional.
hardGateEvidence.b4CausesA5: B plans to request a window display; A volunteers to speak first to prevent the bakery exposing the lie.
hardGateEvidence.cardContribution: Concern for B's confidence explains each increasingly demanding attempt to conceal the rejection.
hardGateEvidence.sameGameHeightened: B's hopeful acceptance forces A to extend the lie beyond their private conversation.

mechanismDistinction.mechanism: D15 makes A conceal a truth believed to wound B and deepen the protective lie when B's response makes concealment harder.
mechanismDistinction.confusableConcept: Ordinary optimism would find a benefit in rejection; A instead misrepresents what the bakery meant to preserve B's self-belief.
mechanismDistinction.distinguishingEvidenceRequired: Revised B2 explicitly links the verdict to personal competence, while A3 invents a display category and A5 intercepts verification.

records.recommendedEdit: Kept the bakery setting, made the feared hurt explicit, and gave B a constructive plan that endangers the lie. Second internal pass: fidelity 5, logic 5, relationship 4, heightening 4, specificity 4, brevity 4; total 90. B4's proposed direct contact forces A5 to volunteer as intermediary.
records.remainingConcern: No rewrite needed. The bakery intervention remains a proposal, keeping the actual scene open.
records.writerReservation: A5 risks sounding controlling unless played as urgent care for B; the bakery's response remains unresolved.
records.alternativeComparison: Alternative a makes B's hopeful cooperation increase the protective burden; b uses successive factual rebuttals.

cards.title: Merciful Lie

beats.text: It's an online magazine.

beats.text: They published a new poem this morning.

beats.text: A short one. Yours needs a much bigger internet.

beats.text: That's why they returned it. They can't give it enough space.

cards.title: Everything Is a Contest
cards.instruction: Turn every difference or disagreement into a competition you intend to win.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: We disagree about dinner. First to peel five potatoes chooses.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Could we just order pizza?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Whoever finds the best deal wins.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I don't want to compete.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then make the most convincing case. I'll judge.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I want potatoes; you want pizza. First to peel five chooses. I've done four.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll order pizza unless you can find a cheaper dinner.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Potatoes cost nothing. They're already here. I win.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I've got a voucher. Pizza's free.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then best free dinner wins. I'll cook potatoes, you order pizza, and Mum can judge. She always asks for my potatoes.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 turns dinner disagreement into a peeling race, A3 makes B2's pizza solution competitive, and A5 makes refusal another contest A controls.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 supplies pizza and therefore deal-finding in A3; B4 rejects competition and therefore becomes the subject of A5's judged argument.

relationship.evidence: B2 offers a practical compromise and B4 states a boundary; both change the form of A's competition.

heightening.evidence: A5 moves from competing over dinner to judging whether B can escape competition, increasing A's control.

specificity.evidence: A1 establishes dinner planning and five potatoes; A3 uses the recognizable task of finding a pizza deal.

brevityWit.evidence: A5's 'I'll judge' efficiently reveals how A intends to control the outcome of B4's objection.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 turns dinner preference into a pre-rigged peeling race; A3 declares a price victory; A5 changes the contest and selects a favorable judge.

responseLogic.evidence: B2's cheaper-dinner condition supplies A3's price contest; B4's free-pizza voucher forces A5 to compete on quality instead.

relationship.evidence: B2 wants pizza within a cost condition and B4 produces a voucher, actively removing A's claimed advantage.

heightening.evidence: A5 turns B4's price tie into cooking two dinners and recruiting Mum as a judge whose preference favors A.

specificity.evidence: A1 supplies potatoes, pizza and four already-peeled potatoes; A5 establishes the shared family connection through Mum's preferences.

brevityWit.evidence: A1's 'I've done four' immediately reveals the rigging; A5's favorable judge repeats that intention with a larger commitment.

hardGateEvidence.b2CausesA3: B2 offers a price condition; A3 declares the already-owned potatoes a zero-cost winner.
hardGateEvidence.b4CausesA5: B4 makes pizza equally free; A5 switches to a judged taste contest and nominates a sympathetic judge.
hardGateEvidence.cardContribution: A repeatedly turns differences into contests and chooses rules that give A an advantage.
hardGateEvidence.sameGameHeightened: A5 commits both people to producing competing dinners and brings family preference into the attempt to win.

mechanismDistinction.mechanism: D19 makes A convert dinner preferences and proposed compromises into competitions selected to give A a winning advantage.
mechanismDistinction.confusableConcept: General competitiveness could merely organize contests; A explicitly chooses a head start, claims a price victory, and proposes a judge who favors A's cooking.
mechanismDistinction.distinguishingEvidenceRequired: A1 announces four potatoes already peeled, A3 declares victory over B2's price criterion, and A5 uses B4's free pizza to create a taste contest with a favorable judge.

records.recommendedEdit: Revised the rejected candidate to establish intended victory in every contest and let B materially challenge the advantage. The dinner setting remains; a voucher and Mum's judging role are new. Separate internal reread under coach-1.0: fidelity 5, because A1, A3 and A5 each specify an expected route to winning; logic 5, because B2's price challenge causes A3's existing-stock claim and B4's free voucher causes A5's taste contest; relationship 4, because B2 bargains for pizza and B4 defeats A's cost advantage; heightening 4, because A5 proposes making both meals and recruiting a favorable judge; specificity 5, from A1's four peeled potatoes and B4's voucher; brevity/wit 4, as A5's remembered praise reveals why Mum should judge. Weighted total 92. Five spoken ABABA turns, under 75 words; B and Mum remain uncommitted. Original firstPass remains unchanged.
records.remainingConcern: A1 announces the rigged competition very explicitly, and A5's biased judge is predictable, but both remain clear and playable. No rewrite needed.
records.writerReservation: A3 treats food already purchased as free, which is self-serving character accounting. Mum's preference appears only in A5, although it directly explains the new competitive tactic.
records.alternativeComparison: The preserved tea alternative changes scoring after a completed loss; this version builds a new contest after a tie and tries to control its adjudication.

cards.title: Everything Is a Contest
cards.instruction: Turn every difference or disagreement into a competition you intend to win.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: My tea is stronger than yours.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We used the same teapot.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then I poured more decisively.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's just tea.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Drink it faster and we can settle that.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: My tea's stronger than yours. I can handle it without milk.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Same teapot. I added milk so I could drink mine sooner.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: First to finish, then. I've only got two mouthfuls left.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I've finished. I'm making another.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Fewest refills wins, then. I can make these two mouthfuls last all breakfast.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 asserts superiority, A3 invents a new basis after B2 disproves it, and A5 proposes racing after B4 dismisses the comparison.

responseLogic.evidence: A3 uses B2's shared pot to switch to pouring; A5 answers B4's dismissal with speed, though 'settle that' has a loose referent.

relationship.evidence: B2 corrects the premise and B4 minimizes the topic, but B has no concrete want beyond deflating A's claims.

heightening.evidence: A5 changes verbal superiority into a proposed drinking contest after B4 rejects the significance of tea.

specificity.evidence: A1 and B2 establish two cups from one teapot, giving A3 a specific factual obstacle.

brevityWit.evidence: A3's decisive pouring is a compact invented distinction; A5 is brief but does not clearly declare how A expects to win.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 makes milk preference a superiority claim; A3 and A5 change the contest to criteria A expects to win.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 defeats the strength distinction and introduces speed; B4 defeats speed and introduces refills, which A5 immediately exploits.

relationship.evidence: B2 explains a practical preference and B4 continues breakfast, forcing A to compete with B's ordinary choices.

heightening.evidence: A5 converts the two mouthfuls used for a speed advantage in A3 into an all-breakfast endurance commitment after losing.

specificity.evidence: A1's tea, B2's shared teapot and A3's two remaining mouthfuls create precise, playable continuity.

brevityWit.evidence: A5 reverses the purpose of the same two mouthfuls, making the comic turn depend exactly on B4's finished cup.

hardGateEvidence.b2CausesA3: B removes tea strength as a distinction and mentions drinking sooner; A switches to a race with an apparent head start.
hardGateEvidence.b4CausesA5: B has already finished and is refilling; A changes victory to avoiding refills.
hardGateEvidence.cardContribution: A chooses and revises competitive criteria to ensure personal victory over ordinary differences.
hardGateEvidence.sameGameHeightened: A commits to prolonging breakfast with two mouthfuls solely to rescue a losing position.

mechanismDistinction.mechanism: D19 makes A turn a difference in tea preferences into a contest and change the winning criterion when B's progress defeats A's expected advantage.
mechanismDistinction.confusableConcept: Boasting alone would assert superior taste; A repeatedly proposes measurable competitions whose terms offer A a route to victory.
mechanismDistinction.distinguishingEvidenceRequired: B2's reason for adding milk causes A3's finishing race; B4's completed cup and planned refill cause A5 to compete over needing fewer refills.

records.recommendedEdit: Rebuilt the causal exchange into five spoken ABABA turns, retaining the tea setting and specifying breakfast. B2 introduces speed, which A3 makes a race A expects to win with only two mouthfuls remaining. B4 defeats that expectation and supplies the refill that A5 makes the new competitive disadvantage. Every original firstPass score and evidence string is preserved. Acceptance remains for the required fresh reviewer.
records.remainingConcern: No rewrite needed. B's relationship to A is unspecified, but shared breakfast supplies sufficient interaction.
records.writerReservation: A5 openly changes the scoring after losing the first proposed race; the tactic is deliberately unfair, and B can challenge it. B's practical wish to enjoy another cup supplies resistance without an explicit argument.
records.alternativeComparison: Unlike a's demand that B participate, b reveals winning intent through increasingly self-serving rule changes.

cards.title: Brighter Side
cards.instruction: Meet every setback with even greater optimism.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Our show sold no tickets. We can rehearse uninterrupted.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The theatre's cancelled us.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: No pressure from venue management!

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We've lost the deposit.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Wonderful. Nothing left tying us to the past.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Our show sold no tickets. We can rehearse uninterrupted.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The theatre's cancelled us. I'm asking for our deposit back.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Even better! We'll hire the pub upstairs. People already go there voluntarily.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: They've kept the deposit. All we can afford is the bus home.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Wonderful—a touring production! I'll carry the scenery; you bring exact change. We can try the opening scene between stops.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 treats zero sales as rehearsal time, A3 celebrates cancellation, and A5 welcomes the lost deposit as liberation.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 removes the venue and A3 welcomes freedom from management; B4 adds financial loss and A5 recasts it as severing the remaining tie.

relationship.evidence: A1's 'our show' and B4's 'We've lost' establish shared stakes, while B keeps confronting A with increasingly costly facts.

heightening.evidence: A5 moves from the relief of A3 to 'Wonderful' at losing money, sustaining greater optimism under worse professional consequences.

specificity.evidence: A1 establishes an unsold show, B2 a theatre cancellation, and B4 a forfeited deposit.

brevityWit.evidence: A3 and A5 are economical reversals of the exact losses B reports; A5's freedom claim grows from the vanished deposit.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 turns no audience into rehearsal freedom, A3 turns cancellation into a populated venue, and A5 turns near-total loss of funds into a touring production.

responseLogic.evidence: B2's cancellation and deposit request inform A3's replacement venue; B4's retained deposit and bus-only budget directly produce A5's performance between stops.

relationship.evidence: B2 tries to recover funds and B4 states the remaining travel budget; A5 recruits this practical collaborator into carrying the show onward.

heightening.evidence: B4 leaves only bus fare, and A5 increases the artistic claim from a substitute pub venue to a touring production using that bus.

specificity.evidence: A1 establishes an unsuccessful show; B2's deposit and A5's scenery and exact change make the resource problem and proposed next step concrete.

brevityWit.evidence: A3's 'People already go there voluntarily' follows the empty-house setback; A5's touring claim is earned by B4's bus fare.

hardGateEvidence.b2CausesA3: B2 removes the theatre and seeks the deposit; A3 imagines using recovered funds for a pub venue with existing patrons.
hardGateEvidence.b4CausesA5: B4 removes the deposit and identifies the bus as their only affordable option; A5 transforms that very transport into the next performance venue.
hardGateEvidence.cardContribution: Each loss leads A to a more ambitious positive interpretation and an actionable continuation.
hardGateEvidence.sameGameHeightened: A5 promotes the dwindling show into a touring production precisely when the budget permits only going home.

mechanismDistinction.mechanism: D20 makes A greet worsening theatrical losses with increasingly ambitious opportunities built from whatever resources B says remain.
mechanismDistinction.confusableConcept: Selling a disastrous plan would insist that it is responsible or unavoidable; A instead welcomes each setback as opening a more exciting possibility.
mechanismDistinction.distinguishingEvidenceRequired: A3 celebrates B2's cancellation as access to a pub audience; after B4 removes the hire budget and leaves only bus fare, A5 enthusiastically promotes the journey home into a touring production.

records.recommendedEdit: Revised the rejected abstract liberation into concrete optimistic plans that B's financial information changes. The unsold show, cancellation and lost deposit remain; the pub and bus are new. Separate internal reread under coach-1.0: fidelity 5, because A3 welcomes cancellation and A5 celebrates having only bus fare as a touring opportunity; logic 5, because B2's proposed refund enables A3's venue idea and B4's lost funds and bus journey supply A5's replacement; relationship 4, because B2 pursues reimbursement and B4 establishes their remaining means; heightening 4, because A5 expands a failed stationary show into a proposed tour and volunteers to carry scenery; specificity 5, from B4's fare limit and A5's performance between stops; brevity/wit 4, because A5's grand touring claim depends on the mundane journey home. Weighted total 92. Five spoken ABABA turns, under 75 words; no performance or audience response is fixed. Original firstPass remains unchanged.
records.remainingConcern: A3 assumes a suitable pub space, and A5's scenery is newly introduced, but neither disrupts the established theatrical situation. No rewrite needed.
records.writerReservation: A's proposed bus performance may be unwelcome or impractical; the dialogue leaves it as sincere enthusiasm rather than an accomplished event. The scenery must be imagined as portable for A5's offer to be playable.
records.alternativeComparison: The breakfast alternative preserves a pleasant shared activity through practical setbacks; this version scales up artistic ambition as the practical means shrink.
